89	          # condition context have errexit suppressed inside, so a plain
90	          # sequence would still push after a failed build.
91	          build_push() {
92	            docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" . && docker push "$IMAGE"
93	          }
94	          retry build_push
95	
96	      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-compatible
97	      # (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new schema. Runs the
98	      # one-off migrate Container Apps Job (provisioned per deploy/README.md).
99	      # `az containerapp job start` only *starts* the execution and returns, so we
100	      # capture the execution name and poll it to a terminal state — the rollout
101	      # below must not begin until the migration has actually SUCCEEDED, and a
102	      # failed migration must abort the deploy (fail-closed) rather than roll the
103	      # apps onto an un-migrated schema.
104	      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
105	        run: |
106	          set -euo pipefail
107	          # Roll the job's image on the template FIRST, then start it with no
108	          # --image override. Passing --image to `job start` replaces the
109	          # container template without the IaC-configured command
110	          # (`sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"`), so the execution
111	          # falls back to the image's default CMD (uvicorn) and never migrates.
112	          # Updating the template preserves that command (mirrors the api/worker
113	          # `az containerapp update --image` steps below).
114	          # Both az calls are retried (#539): the containerapp extension crashes
115	          # with KeyError: 'properties' on transient ARM errors, masking them.
116	          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
117	          retry az containerapp job update \
118	            --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
119	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
120	            --image "$IMAGE"
121	          exec_name=""
122	          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
123	            exec_name=$(az containerapp job start \
124	              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
125	              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
126	              --query name -o tsv) && break
127	            echo "::warning::job start failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in $(( attempt * 30 ))s (#539)"
128	            (( attempt < 3 )) && sleep $(( attempt * 30 ))
129	          done
130	          if [[ -z "$exec_name" ]]; then
131	            echo "::error::could not start the migration job after 3 attempts."; exit 1
132	          fi
133	          echo "Started migration execution: $exec_name"
134	          # Poll to a terminal state. Besides the 15-min wall-clock cap, bound the
135	          # number of *consecutive* empty/unexpected statuses: a control-plane
136	          # hiccup or a CLI status-field rename would otherwise leave the loop
137	          # polling a status it never recognises until the full deadline, tying up
138	          # the prod concurrency group with no signal (#397). A recognised
139	          # in-progress status resets the counter; `|| true` keeps a transient
140	          # query failure a retry (counted as unknown) rather than a hard step
141	          # abort under `set -e`.
142	          deadline=$(( SECONDS + 900 ))  # 15-minute cap
143	          unknown=0
144	          unknown_max=18  # ~3 min of consecutive empty/unexpected status → abort
145	          while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
146	            status=$(az containerapp job execution list \
147	              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
148	              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
149	              --query "[?name=='$exec_name'].properties.status | [0]" -o tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
150	            echo "migration status: ${status:-<pending>} (unknown streak: $unknown)"
151	            case "$status" in
152	              Succeeded) echo "Migration succeeded."; exit 0 ;;
153	              Failed|Degraded|Stopped) echo "::error::Migration $status — aborting before app rollout."; exit 1 ;;
154	              Running|Processing|Pending) unknown=0 ;;
155	              *)
156	                unknown=$(( unknown + 1 ))
157	                if (( unknown >= unknown_max )); then
158	                  echo "::error::Migration status empty/unexpected ('${status:-<empty>}') $unknown times in a row — aborting before app rollout."
159	                  exit 1
160	                fi
161	                ;;
162	            esac
163	            sleep 10
164	          done
165	          echo "::error::Timed out waiting for migration to complete."; exit 1
166	
167	      # Both rolls are retried and then VERIFIED against the live template
168	      # (#539): the extension can crash while *rendering* a response, so the
169	      # step's exit code alone doesn't prove the app is on the new image.
170	      - name: Deploy API
171	        run: |
172	          set -euo pipefail
173	          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
174	          retry az containerapp update \
175	            --name "${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
176	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
177	            --image "$IMAGE"
178	          live=$(az containerapp show \
179	            --name "${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
180	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
181	            --query "properties.template.containers[0].image" -o tsv)
182	          [[ "$live" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::API image mismatch after update: $live"; exit 1; }
183	
184	      - name: Deploy worker
185	        run: |
186	          set -euo pipefail
187	          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
188	          retry az containerapp update \
189	            --name "${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
190	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
191	            --image "$IMAGE"
192	          live=$(az containerapp show \
193	            --name "${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
194	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
195	            --query "properties.template.containers[0].image" -o tsv)
196	          [[ "$live" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::worker image mismatch after update: $live"; exit 1; }
197	
198	  frontend:
199	    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to Container App
200	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
201	    environment: production
202	    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed/aborted
203	    # migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against an un-rolled
204	    # or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
205	    needs: backend
206	    steps:
207	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
208	
209	      # Same fail-fast as the backend job (#539 post-mortem) — this is the var
210	      # whose absence burned deploys #1/#2/#4.
211	      - name: Preflight — required repo vars
212	        run: |
213	          set -euo pipefail
214	          fail=0
215	          for pair in "AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP=${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
216	                      "FRONTEND_APP_NAME=${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}"; do
217	            [[ -n "${pair#*=}" ]] || { echo "::error::repo variable ${pair%%=*} is not set"; fail=1; }
218	          done
219	          exit $fail
220	
221	      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
222	        uses: azure/login@v3
223	        with:
224	          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
225	          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
226	          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
227	
228	      - name: Log in to GHCR
229	        uses: docker/login-action@v4
230	        with:
231	          registry: ghcr.io
232	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
233	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
234	
235	      # One generic image (ADR 0028) — nothing baked in. Auth config + the /api
236	      # proxy upstream are injected at runtime by the Container App env
237	      # (DATAQ_AUTH_* / DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM in deploy/terraform/azure/frontend.tf), so
238	      # there are NO VITE_* build args here and no per-environment rebuild. amd64
239	      # only (ACA is amd64); the multi-arch :latest is published by
240	      # publish-images.yml for the BYOL/eval path.
241	      - name: Build + push frontend image to GHCR
242	        run: |
243	          set -euo pipefail
244	          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
245	          # && chain — same errexit-suppression reasoning as the backend build.
246	          build_push() {
247	            docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE_FRONTEND" frontend && docker push "$IMAGE_FRONTEND"
248	          }
249	          retry build_push
250	
251	      # Retried + verified like the API/worker rolls; on the third failure one
252	      # last attempt runs with --debug so the ARM response the extension masks
253	      # (KeyError: 'properties', #539 — Deploys #1/#2) finally lands in the log.
254	      - name: Deploy frontend
255	        run: |
256	          set -euo pipefail
257	          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
258	          update() {
259	            az containerapp update \
260	              --name "${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}" \
261	              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
262	              --image "$IMAGE_FRONTEND" "$@"
263	          }
264	          if ! retry update; then
265	            echo "::warning::final attempt with --debug to surface the masked ARM error (#539)"
266	            update --debug
267	          fi
268	          live=$(az containerapp show \
269	            --name "${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}" \
270	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
271	            --query "properties.template.containers[0].image" -o tsv)
272	          [[ "$live" == "$IMAGE_FRONTEND" ]] || { echo "::error::frontend image mismatch after update: $live"; exit 1; }

input.content:
name: Deploy (AWS)

# Manual-only (workflow_dispatch), mirroring deploy.yml's posture: the Azure
# stack is primary prod, so the AWS parallel deployment rolls only on an
# explicit dispatch — never on push.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      image_tag:
        description: "Image tag to build + deploy (blank → aws-<commit SHA>, an immutable tag)"
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: deploy-aws-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

# OIDC federated login to AWS (no stored access keys — deploy/terraform/aws/
# github_oidc.tf trusts exactly repo:<this repo>:environment:production).
# packages:write lets the GITHUB_TOKEN push both images to GHCR (ADR 0023);
# ECS pulls them anonymously (public packages), so no registry credential
# exists on the AWS side.
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
  packages: write

env:
  # `aws-<sha>` — NOT the bare `<sha>` (owned by the Azure deploy.yml) and NOT
  # `main-<sha>` (owned by publish-images.yml, which skips docs-only merges):
  # this workflow always builds its own immutable tag so the migrate task, api,
  # worker, and frontend all roll the exact build this run produced (#382).
  IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
  IMAGE_FRONTEND: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
  # Statically named by deploy/terraform/aws/ (the IAM policy's
  # RegisterTaskDefinition grant is scoped to the dataq-app-* families, so
  # these are contract, not convention).
  API_SERVICE: dataq-app-api
  WORKER_SERVICE: dataq-app-worker
  FRONTEND_SERVICE: dataq-app-frontend
  MIGRATE_FAMILY: dataq-app-migrate

jobs:
  backend:
    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Fail fast on unset repo vars/secrets (#539 post-mortem, same rule as
      # deploy.yml): never let an empty value masquerade as a transient error
      # three steps later.
      - name: Preflight — required repo vars + secrets
        env:
          DEPLOY_ROLE: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          fail=0
          for pair in "AWS_REGION=${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}" \
                      "ECS_CLUSTER=${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                      "AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN=$DEPLOY_ROLE"; do
            [[ -n "${pair#*=}" ]] || { echo "::error::${pair%%=*} is not set"; fail=1; }
          done
          exit $fail

      - name: AWS login (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Retried (#539): a registry blip on the base-image pull or the GHCR push
      # shouldn't fail the deploy — a re-run hits the local layer cache.
      - name: Build + push backend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          # && chain, not two statements: functions called from retry's
          # condition context have errexit suppressed inside, so a plain
          # sequence would still push after a failed build.
          build_push() {
            docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" . && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-
      # compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new
      # schema. Unlike ACA jobs, an ECS task definition carries no separately
      # stored command to clobber — the migrate family's command lives IN the
      # definition — so re-registering with only the image swapped preserves it.
      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh

          # Register a new migrate revision on the new image. describe → strip
          # the register-rejected output-only fields → register.
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$MIGRATE_FAMILY" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          register() {
            aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
          }
          migrate_arn=$(retry register)
          echo "Registered migrate task definition: $migrate_arn"

          # The one-off task runs with the api service's exact network shape
          # (same subnets/SG → same RDS reachability), read live rather than
          # duplicated into repo vars that would drift from the Terraform.
          netcfg=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                     --services "$API_SERVICE" \
                     --query 'services[0].networkConfiguration' --output json)

          run_task() {
            aws ecs run-task --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --task-definition "$migrate_arn" \
              --launch-type FARGATE \
              --network-configuration "$netcfg" \
              --query 'tasks[0].taskArn' --output text
          }
          task_arn=$(retry run_task)
          echo "Started migration task: $task_arn"

          # Fail-closed: the rollout below must not begin until the migration
          # has actually SUCCEEDED (exit 0). `aws ecs wait tasks-stopped` polls
          # 6s × 100 (10 min) and exits 255 on waiter timeout.
          aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" --tasks "$task_arn"
          state=$(aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" --tasks "$task_arn" \
                    --query 'tasks[0].[containers[0].exitCode, stopCode, stoppedReason]' --output json)
          exit_code=$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$state")
          if [[ "$exit_code" != "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Migration failed (exit=${exit_code}, $(jq -r '.[1] + ": " + .[2]' <<<"$state")) — aborting before app rollout."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Migration succeeded."

      # Register new api/worker revisions on the new image and roll both, then
      # WAIT for the deployments to complete — the step's exit code must mean
      # "the services are actually running the new image", not "the API call
      # was accepted" (the deploy.yml #539 verify rule, ECS-shaped).
      - name: Deploy API + worker
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          roll() {
            local family=$1
            local td new_td arn
            td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
                   --query taskDefinition --output json)
            new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
              '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
               | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                     .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
              <<<"$td")
            register() {
              aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
                --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
            }
            arn=$(retry register)
            update() {
              aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                --service "$family" --task-definition "$arn" \
                --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
            }
            retry update
            echo "$family -> $arn"
          }
          roll "$API_SERVICE"
          roll "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # services-stable polls 15s × 40 (10 min); exits 255 on timeout, so a
          # stuck rollout (crash-looping new revision) fails the deploy here.
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # Verify the primary deployment really is the new image (not merely
          # stable on the OLD one after a circuit-breaker rollback).
          for svc in "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"; do
            live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                        --services "$svc" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
            live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                         --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
            [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::$svc image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }
          done

  frontend:
    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to ECS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed or
    # aborted migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against
    # an un-rolled or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
    needs: backend
    env:
      # Job-level so the roll step below sees the frontend image as $IMAGE and
      # the shared roll logic stays identical to the backend job's.
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: AWS login (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # One generic image (ADR 0028) — nothing baked in. Auth config + the /api
      # proxy upstream are injected at runtime by the task definition env
      # (DATAQ_AUTH_* / DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM in deploy/terraform/aws/ecs.tf), so
      # there are NO VITE_* build args and no per-environment rebuild. amd64
      # only (the Fargate tasks are amd64); the multi-arch :latest is published
      # by publish-images.yml for the BYOL/eval path.
      - name: Build + push frontend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          build_push() {
            docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" frontend && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      - name: Deploy frontend
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          register() {
            aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
          }
          arn=$(retry register)
          update() {
            aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --service "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --task-definition "$arn" \
              --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
          }
          retry update
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE"
          live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                      --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)

                       --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
          [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::frontend image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }

      # Post-deploy smoke through the real public surface (CloudFront). The URL
      # is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730),
      # so this runs only when the optional AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var is set —
      # skipping is loudly logged, never silent.
      - name: Smoke (public surface)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="${{ vars.AWS_FRONTEND_URL }}"
          if [[ -z "$url" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var not set — skipping the public-surface smoke."
            exit 0
          fi
          for path_want in "/healthz 200" "/ 200" "/api/v1/me 401"; do
            path=${path_want% *}; want=${path_want#* }
            got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "${url%/}${path}")
            [[ "$got" == "$want" ]] || { echo "::error::smoke: ${path} returned ${got}, wanted ${want}"; exit 1; }

# Shared ECS deploy helpers for deploy-aws.yml — source this, don't execute it.
# Requires: aws + jq on PATH, and scripts/ci/retry.sh sourced first (retry()).
#
# One implementation of the describe → image-swap → register → update →
# wait → verify roll, so the migrate, api/worker, and frontend steps cannot
# silently diverge (PR #1365 review). Values are returned via shell variables
# assigned INSIDE the retried functions — retry() logs ::warning:: lines to
# stdout, so `var=$(retry fn)` would swallow them into the captured value.

# Register a new revision of task-definition family $1 with its (single)
# container's image swapped to $2. Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN.
ecs_register_revision() {
  local family=$1 image=$2 td new_td
  td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
         --query taskDefinition --output json)
  # del(): the output-only fields describe returns that register rejects.
  new_td=$(jq --arg img "$image" \
    '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
     | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
           .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
    <<<"$td")
  _ecs_register() {
    ECS_REGISTERED_ARN=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
      --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
  }
  retry _ecs_register
}

# Roll service $2 on cluster $1 to image $3 (service name == family name in
# this stack). Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN to the revision it rolled to.
ecs_roll_service() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3
  ecs_register_revision "$service" "$image"
  _ecs_update() {
    aws ecs update-service --cluster "$cluster" --service "$service" \
      --task-definition "$ECS_REGISTERED_ARN" \
      --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
  }
  retry _ecs_update
  echo "$service -> $ECS_REGISTERED_ARN"
}

# Wait for the listed services on cluster $1 to stabilise. TWO waiter laps
# (each 15s x 40 = 10 min): a perfectly normal rollout can exceed one lap
# because the ALB target group's default 300s deregistration drain sits on
# the deployment-complete path — a converging deploy must not spuriously
# fail on the waiter's fixed cap (PR #1365 review).
ecs_wait_stable() {
  local cluster=$1
  shift
  if ! aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"; then
    echo "::warning::services-stable waiter lap 1 timed out — one more lap (ALB drain can push a normal rollout past 10 min)"
    aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"
  fi
}

# Verify service $2's PRIMARY deployment on cluster $1 actually runs image $3:
# an ECS deployment-circuit-breaker rollback to the old image reports stable,
# and "stable on the old code" must fail the deploy, not pass it.
ecs_verify_image() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3 live_td live_img
  live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "$cluster" --services "$service" \
              --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
  live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
               --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
  if [[ "$live_img" != "$image" ]]; then
    echo "::error::$service image mismatch after rollout: $live_img (wanted $image)"
    return 1
  fi
}

The file's own docstring had documented that exact hazard; the lesson recorded is to check the **exit code**, not the "N passed" line.)))))))) |

All three stages are done — full E2E green on AWS and `deploy-aws.yml` shipped and validated with a real production deploy.

## 1. Cognito user

Created `royarijit1995+aws-e2e@gmail.com` ("AWS E2E", email verified, non-admin). It signed in through the hosted UI and was provisioned via the userinfo fallback, exactly as the OIDC track predicted. I rotated its password to an unknown random afterward (the test password had to pass through the transcript) — use Forgot-password on the sign-in page to claim it.

## 2. Connections, suites, checks, Secrets Manager, E2E

But first, a blocker the post-apply smoke couldn't see: **the AWS worker had never started**. Celery hard-rejects a `rediss://` URL lacking `ssl_cert_reqs`, so it crash-looped since the apply (25+ dead tasks), and the api's dispatch path would have died identically. Filed **#1361**, fixed in [#1362](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1362) (`?ssl_cert_reqs=required` — verified as the one spelling celery/kombu/redis-py all accept), applied, rolled, and confirmed live: `celery ready` over TLS to ElastiCache. Generic follow-up filed as #1363.

Then the E2E, all through the live app (credentials piped inline from the local-mirror OpenBao, never printed; Azure CLI was logged out):

- **Snowflake + Unity Catalog connections created** → credentials landed in **AWS Secrets Manager** as `dataq/conn-snowflake-retail-dev-02d99a91` and `dataq/conn-unity-catalog-retail-dev-dd5ca985`; both Test Connections green against the real warehouses.
- **Suites + checks authored** (not-null, row-count, freshness monitors, one deliberate FAIL).
- **Runs executed by the AWS worker:** Snowflake `succeeded` 2/4 — a real freshness WARN at 470h and the deliberate FAIL failing as designed; UC `succeeded` **3/3** (freshness 183.6h) after I corrected my own guessed column name (which produced a properly classified per-check `error` — the error path works too). All rendered correctly in the UI.

One more find along the way: **sign-out on Cognito lands on a raw "Client does not exist" 400** and the hosted-UI session survives (silent re-auth as the old user). Filed as **#1364** — Cognito's `/logout` isn't standards-conformant; Azure AD is, which is why prod never showed it.

## 3. deploy-aws.yml — shipped and tested

[#1365](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1365) merged: OIDC role login, immutable `aws-<sha>` tags (disjoint from the Azure and publish-images namespaces), migrate RunTask gated on exit 0 using the api service's live network config, rolls via a shared `scripts/ci/ecs_roll.sh` that verifies the primary deployment's image (a circuit-breaker rollback fails the run), and a CloudFront smoke gated on the new `AWS_FRONTEND_URL` repo var. The review caught four real defects pre-merge (the literal-`None` ARN trap on run-task placement failures, waiter-vs-ALB-drain timing, triplicated roll logic, no curl timeout) — all fixed.

Then dispatched for real: [run 31909137435](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31909137435) went green first try — migrate exit 0, all three services `COMPLETED` on `aws-8f08652b`, smoke 200/200/401, and healthz confirmed live afterward.

content.text:
## Parity today (after this session)

| Capability | Azure (primary prod) | AWS | Parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| App hosting (api internal / worker+beat / frontend public / migrate) | ACA ×3 + migrate job | ECS Fargate ×3 + migrate task | ✅ full |
| Public HTTPS surface | frontend ACA ingress | CloudFront → ALB → nginx | ✅ (gap: #1355 origin secret — Azure has no analogous hole) |
| Database | shared `dataq-pg-wus3` Flexible Server | RDS `db.t4g.micro` (dedicated) | ✅ |
| Broker / rate limits | self-hosted Redis ACA | ElastiCache TLS+auth | ✅ (fixed today — the worker had never started before #1362) |
| Secrets | Key Vault (UAMI) | Secrets Manager (task-role) | ✅ — proven today: connection creds landed as `dataq/conn-*` via the app |
| Auth | Azure AD via generic OIDC | Cognito via the same `OidcBearerScheme` + userinfo fallback | ✅ sign-in; ❌ **sign-out broken (#1364)**; only 2 users exist vs Azure's demo cohort |
| CI/CD deploy | `deploy.yml` | `deploy-aws.yml` — **validated live today** | ✅ |
| Suite execution against real warehouses | SF / UC / ADLS / S3-MinIO / Iceberg configured | **SF + UC configured and green today**; other types work but aren't configured | 🟡 config, not code |
| MCP `/mcp` | live, 8 tools | 401 gate verified; no full tool E2E yet | 🟡 |
| Alert channels (Teams/Slack/email) | wired, secrets in KV | seam present; `EMAIL_FROM` empty, no channel secrets set | ❌ config |
| Observability | App Insights: OTel spans + exported logs + KQL | **CloudWatch container logs only — no span/APM exporter at all** (`tracing.py` is Azure-exporter-only, #525) | ❌ biggest real gap |
| Infra alerting (dead-poll, health) | Azure Monitor alert rules | none (no CloudWatch alarms) | ❌ |
| Durability posture | prod-ish | eval-grade: `backup_retention=1`, no deletion protection, `skip_final_snapshot`, single-AZ, public subnets/no NAT | ❌ deliberate cost choices |

## What a full Azure→AWS switch still needs (app hosting only)

**New resources / code:**
1. **APM/tracing target** — the one code seam: an OTLP/ADOT (or X-Ray) exporter branch in `backend/app/core/tracing.py` + collector/endpoint resources, or you lose #525's spans and the log export entirely. Plus CloudWatch alarms replacing Azure Monitor (service health, beat watchdog, 5xx).
2. **Custom domain** — Route 53 + ACM cert on CloudFront (today's URL is the default `*.cloudfront.net`; every OIDC redirect URI, webhook, and MCP client config keys off it, so pick the domain *before* migrating users).
3. **Email/alert channel config** — SES (or SMTP) + `EMAIL_FROM` + channel secrets (`channel-email-password`, Teams/Slack webhook URLs) into Secrets Manager.
4. **#1355** — CloudFront origin secret verified at nginx (until then any CloudFront distribution can origin-point at the ALB).
5. **Prod-grade durability** — RDS backups ≥7d + deletion protection + final snapshot, ElastiCache snapshots, ideally private subnets + NAT (or VPC endpoints) and multi-AZ; all currently traded away for cost.

**Migration work (no new code):**
6. **Data** — `pg_dump` Azure PG → RDS (users, PATs, suites, checks, run history), then **re-mint every per-connection secret** into Secrets Manager — the one-credential-becomes-N-secrets trap that caused the 3-week dead-connections incident.
7. **Identity** — recreate users in Cognito (no import of Azure AD identities; `aad_object_id`/`oidc_issuer` self-heal on next login since #1340, but each human needs a Cognito account) and **fix #1364 first** — you can't run prod on a sign-out that 400s and silently re-authenticates.
8. **Webhook re-point** — ADF/Airflow/dbt callback URLs → the new domain, secrets into Secrets Manager.
9. Confirm `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3` against one real logged XFF, and #1338 (runbook docs).

Everything else — GX engine, orchestration abstraction, secret-store seam, alerting seam, GHCR images — is already cloud-neutral and needs nothing. The honest summary: **functional parity is essentially there as of today; what's missing for a *switch* is observability, identity/domain migration, and durability hardening — config and ops, not application code, except the tracing exporter.**

18	 *                    OIDC auth client (oidc-client-ts — ADR 0028/#504) drives
19	 *                    redirect-flow login + token acquisition.

22	 *                    never sees, so there is nothing else to configure here.
23	 * - 'dev_bypass'   — ONLY when `mode:'bypass'` is explicitly set. Fail-closed:
24	 *                    never inferred from missing config. Renders a fixed dev user.
25	 * - 'unconfigured' — anything else. AuthGate shows a setup-needed banner.
26	 *
27	 * The `otp` value is one half of a **pair of coordinated selectors** (ADR 0032
28	 * decision 2): the backend infers its own mode from `AUTH_EMAIL_*` + the signup
29	 * allowlist and never reads this one. Set both or neither — this alone yields a
30	 * code form whose endpoints 503.

# SES — the email alert channel (#1368), the AWS-native counterpart of the
# SMTP creds the Azure stack keeps in Key Vault. Everything here is gated on
# var.alert_email: empty (the default) creates nothing and the app's email
# channel stays off (config.py enables it only when EMAIL_TO + EMAIL_USERNAME
# + EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME are all set).
#
# Sandbox posture, stated honestly: a fresh SES account can only send FROM and
# TO verified identities, so alert_email is both the sender and the sole
# recipient — fine for a single-operator deployment; production fan-out needs
# an SES production-access request (an AWS support form, not Terraform).
#
# The identity requires a ONE-TIME human step: SES emails a verification link
# to alert_email at create time, and sends fail with "Email address is not
# verified" until it is clicked. Check with:
#   aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities <alert_email>

resource "aws_ses_email_identity" "alert" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  email = var.alert_email
}

# Dedicated IAM user for SMTP: SES SMTP credentials ARE an IAM access key —
# the username is the key id and the password is Terraform's derived
# ses_smtp_password_v4 (the documented SigV4 derivation, region-specific).
# Scoped to SendRawEmail only (what SMTP submission uses), from this identity.
resource "aws_iam_user" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name  = "dataq-app-ses-smtp"
  tags  = { Name = "dataq-app-ses-smtp" }
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  statement {
    actions   = ["ses:SendRawEmail"]
    resources = [aws_ses_email_identity.alert[0].arn]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_user_policy" "ses_smtp" {
  count  = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name   = "dataq-app-ses-smtp-send"
  user   = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ses_smtp[0].json
}

resource "aws_iam_access_key" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  user  = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
}

# The SMTP password goes into Secrets Manager UNDER THE APP PREFIX
# (dataq/channel-email-password): the task env's EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME
# already names `channel-email-password`, which the app resolves through its
# own SecretStore (SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager + AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX
# = dataq/) at send time — same read path as every connection credential, no
# extra task-definition secret injection.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "channel_email_password" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name  = "dataq/channel-email-password"
  # The app's sweep/rotation owns secrets under dataq/, but this one is
  # infra-owned: recovery_window 0 so a destroy/recreate cycle doesn't collide
  # with a soft-deleted name.
  recovery_window_in_days = 0
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "channel_email_password" {
  count         = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.channel_email_password[0].id
  secret_string = aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].ses_smtp_password_v4
}

locals {
  # Consumed by ecs.tf's app env. Region-matched SMTP endpoint; STARTTLS :587
  # (the app's email_smtp_port default).
  ses_smtp_host  = "email-smtp.${var.aws_region}.amazonaws.com"
  email_username = var.alert_email == "" ? "" : aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].id
}

input.old_string: ## State encryption
input.new_string:
## Rolling task-definition changes (env vars, sidecars)

The api/worker/frontend task definitions carry `lifecycle { ignore_changes =
[container_definitions] }` (CI rolls images out-of-band), so a Terraform-side
change to env vars or sidecar containers is **silently ignored by a plain
apply**. To roll one:

```bash
tofu apply -replace=aws_ecs_task_definition.api ... # forces a new revision from config
aws ecs update-service --cluster dataq-app --service dataq-app-api \
  --task-definition dataq-app-api --force-new-deployment   # family name → latest revision
```

The services also ignore `task_definition`, hence the explicit
`update-service`. Later CI deploys copy the LIVE definition and swap only the
image, so the change persists across deploy-aws.yml runs.

## State encryption

# Register a new revision of task-definition family $1 with the APP
# container's image swapped to $2. Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN.
#
# "The app container" = the essential one, selected BY PREDICATE rather than
# by position: the api/worker task defs also carry an essential=false
# adot-collector sidecar (#1369), and a positional [0] would stamp the app
# image onto whichever container happens to be listed first (PR #1371 review).
ecs_register_revision() {
  local family=$1 image=$2 td new_td
  td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
         --query taskDefinition --output json)
  # del(): the output-only fields describe returns that register rejects.
  new_td=$(jq --arg img "$image" \
    '.containerDefinitions |= map(if .essential == true then .image = $img else . end)
     | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
           .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
    <<<"$td")
